Subject: Quick ask — short 3-day uplift + pricing question

Hi Rishi / team,

We're going into a small, timeboxed marketing push the week of July 12 and expect an acute spike in LLM traffic for roughly 72 hours. Our baseline commit is 5M tokens/month but this will need a short, high-volume burst.

Can you share:
- A recommended commercial approach for a 3-day ephemeral uplift (20M tokens/day peak).
- Whether Redwood can offer a temporary effective rate ceiling for that window (we want to avoid surprise invoice cliffs) and any pathway to credit a portion of the uplift if we convert to a commit post-campaign.
- Timing for PO/invoice and any SOC 2 / audit evidence you’ll need for procurement.

Attached is a forecast and a rough timeline (brightcart_q3_forecast.xlsx).

Appreciate a quick runbook — we need to confirm budget by EOD Friday.

Thanks,
Olly Chen
Head of Product Partnerships
BrightCart

BrightCart (external)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Olly Chen <olly@brightcart.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 18:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Quick ask — short 3-day uplift + pricing question

Hi Olly — thanks for the forecast and the heads-up. We can support this; two viable commercial patterns that are common: a) Ephemeral uplift add-on (metered at a higher uplift multiplier) billed immediately, or b) Provisional escrow / true-up where uplift is measured and then partially credited if converted into a committed reserved capacity within an agreed window.

Quick proposal for BrightCart to consider (first-pass):
- Baseline: 5M tokens/month committed.
- Ephemeral uplift option: up to 20M tokens/day for a 3-day window. Uplift billing rate = standard hosted per-token rate * 1.8 (applies only to tokens above baseline for that billing period).
- Conversion credit: if BrightCart converts the uplift into a sustained commit within 60 days, we will credit 50% of the uplift charges back as a one-time credit against the first month of the new commit.
- Discount incentive: sign PO within 14 days of campaign -> 10% discount on uplift charges.
- Invoice timing: uplift billed in the next invoice cycle; if you need net-30 PO timing we can route through sales finance.

Attachments: I’m attaching a short term sheet (Proposed_terms_ephemeral_uplift_v1.pdf) outlining these options and the data points our finance/legal will need.

A couple of operational notes: prefix caching and KV reuse can reduce actual tokens billed; if you share expected prompt templates we can estimate billed tokens more precisely. Also copy Laura (sales ops) on procurement timelines.

If that looks close to what you need, we can fast-track a tighter two-page SOW and finalize PO route.

Best,
Rishi
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

Rishi / Karthik — looping you in with internal commercial suggestions before we lock a number with BrightCart. My read: compete on predictability and conversion credit rather than deep uplift discounts. Proposed counter:

- Reduce uplift multiplier to 1.5x (we still capture margin at peak but look more palatable).
- Increase conversion credit to 60% of uplift charges if converted to a commit within 60 days.
- Offer a 15% early-PO discount on the uplift (if they sign within 10 business days) instead of the 10% we proposed.
- Add a granular invoice timing note: we can issue an interim prepay invoice for the uplift if procurement needs a PO-to-invoice match before campaign start; finance will accept prepay or next-cycle billing.

We should also confirm SOC 2 evidence (procurement asked) — legal can provide the SOC 2 Type II report and the auditor contact for a quick attestation.

If you both agree, I’ll send the customer a tightened terms PDF and the procurement checklist.

Laura Bennett
Head of Commercial Ops — Redwood Inference

2) Invoice timing: we prefer a single invoice after campaign close rather than prepay — can you accommodate net-30 on that invoice?

Procurement also asked for SOC 2 Type II evidence and the auditor contact for a short attestation call. If you can send the final two-page SOW and the procurement checklist today we’ll route a PO and try to meet the early-PO discount window.

If that’s all good, we’re ready to proceed — we’ll aim to sign the PO within the 10-business-day window to capture the 15% uplift discount.
